## **ORDER** 

The present Petition has been filed by Serentica Renewables India Private Limited (SRIPL), seeking appropriate direction(s) to CTUIL to approve SRIPL’s application dated 16.10.2025 seeking change of source, in terms of Regulation 9.3 of the CERC (Connectivity and General Network Access to the inter-State Transmission System) Regulations, 2022, as amended (“GNA Regulations”). 

## **2.** The Petitioner has made the following prayers vide the instant Petition: 

_(a) Approve SRIPL’s change of renewable energy source Applications dated 16.10.2025 under Regulation 9.3 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to the inter-State Transmission System) Regulations, 2022;_ 

_(b) Pass such other order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may consider deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case._ 

**3.** The Petitioner has also sought interim reliefs vide the Petition as below: 

   - _(a) Injunct CTUIL from taking any coercive steps against SRIPL including revocation of SRIPL’s Connectivity granted vide Connectivity Application No. 2200000610 dated 21.07.2025 and Connectivity Application No. 2200000641 dated 21.07.2025 in terms of Regulation 11(A) and 11(B) of the GNA Regulations and from encashing the Bank Guarantees dated 29.02.2024 and 13.03.2024 submitted in lieu of land, as well as Conn-BG1, Conn-BG2, and Conn-BG3;_ 

   - _(b) Direct CTUIL to not create any third-party rights or allocate SRIPL’s Connectivity quantum to any other entity, such that SRIPL’s application seeking change of source is not rendered infructuous;_ 

   - (c) _Pass such other order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may consider deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case_ . 

**4.** The matter was called for a hearing on 19.05.2026. During the course of the hearing, learned counsel for the Petitioner, SRIPL, while submitting that the Respondent, CTUIL, has already allowed the Petitioner’s change of source application, sought liberty to file an affidavit to place on record the said development along with permission to withdraw the present Petition as it had become infructuous. Considering the above, the Commission permitted the Petitioner to file its affidavit thereof, and subject thereto, the matter was reserved for order. 

**==> picture [23 x 18] intentionally omitted <==**

**Order in Petition Number 227/MP/2026** 

Page **2**

(CTUIL) vide its letter dated 30.04.2026, had approved the Petitioner's change of source application dated 16.10.2025. Since the change in fuel source application has been approved by CTUIL, the present Petition has become infructuous. Accordingly, the Petitioner, without prejudice to its rights and remedies available under law, seeks leave to withdraw the present Petition. 

**6.** In view of the affidavit filed by the Petitioner and the submissions of learned counsels for the Petitioner and CTUIL made during the hearing of the matter, the Petitioner is permitted to withdraw the present Petition. 

**7.** Petition No. 227/MP/2026 is disposed of in terms of the above.

4. The matter was further listed for hearing on 22.5.2026. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioners submitted that since the Detailed Procedure under Regulation 11A(6)(c) of the GNA Regulations had not been notified at the time of filing of the instant Petition, the Petitioners had approached CTUIL _vide_ letter dated 3.3.2026 for approval of the transaction. However, since no reply was received from CTUIL, the Petitioners were constrained to file the present Petition. The learned counsel further submitted that AETPL holds 51% shareholding in both AMPIN C&I and AEUPL, thereby exercising ‘control’ over both entities in terms of Section 2(27) of the Companies Act, 2013. Accordingly, AMPIN C&I 13 will continue to remain a step-down subsidiary of AETPL, and AETPL will continue to exercise ‘control’ over AMPIN C&I 13. According to the Petitioners, there is no change in ‘control’ in the present transaction, and the rigours of Regulation 11A(6) of the GNA Regulations are not attracted. The learned counsel further clarified that the Petitioners are not seeking any advance ruling from the Commission, nor are they seeking to dilute, relax, or circumvent the promoter/control requirements under Regulation 11A(6). The learned counsel further submitted that in terms of Regulation 11A(6) and CTUIL’s letter dated 24.4.2026, it is clear that CTUIL’s permission is not required in cases where there is no change in ‘control’, therefore, the Commission may dispose of the present Petition, holding that there is no change in control and in line with CTUIL’s letter dated 24.4.2026. The learned counsel for the

Respondent/CTUIL _inter alia_ submitted that the Petition seeks a general, forwardlooking pronouncement on how Regulation 11A(6) ought to apply to a class of intragroup restructurings, so as to secure advance clarity for the Petitioners’ proposed transaction structure. The Petition, in substance, seeks an advance ruling on intra-group transfers under Regulation 11A(6), and not redress against any identified _lis inter_ parties. The Petition substantially invites an advisory jurisdiction which the statute does

grantee itself, and if it does, only then does the connectivity grantee, such as the AMPIN C&I 13 herein, require approaching CTUIL for its approval.  In response, the learned counsel for the Petitioners submitted that the Commission may dispose of the present Petition by taking on record his submission that, in terms of the CTUIL’s letter dated 24.4.2026 and the reply dated 15.5.2026, there is no change in control in the present case, attracting the requirement of CTUIL’s prior approval under Regulation 11A(6). The learned counsel sought liberty to file his memo of arguments/ additional note of arguments to this effect. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsels for the parties and the representative of CTUIL, the Commission permitted the Petitioner to file its additional note of argument/memo of arguments.

5. The Petitioners, _vide_ its Memo dated 8.6.2026, have submitted that CTUIL`s prior approval under Regulation 11A(6)  is required only if the proposed transaction  results in any ‘change in control’  of the connectivity grantee. However, in the present case, there is no change in control, since the ultimate parent company, i.e., AMPIN Energy Transition Pvt.  Ltd, would continue to exercise control over the connectivity grantee even after the proposed transfer from Petitioner No. 2 to Petitioner No. 3, both of which are subsidiaries of AETPL. Therefore, neither Regulation 11A(6) nor Clause 16 of the Detailed Procedure would be applicable in the present case. The Petitioners have further submitted that CTUIL, in its letter dated 24.4.2026, addressed to all connectivity grantees in the Northern Region, has itself admitted and clarified that in cases where there is no ‘Change in Control’, prior approval of CTUIL is not required under Regulation 11A(6).   The Petitioners have further submitted that CTUIL, in its reply, also has alluded to the fact that Regulation 11A(6) prescribes that the original promoter/ group that applies for and is granted connectivity must retain control over the Connectivity Grantee up to the COD.

6. Accordingly, in light of the CTUIL`s stand in its letter dated 24.4.2026 and reply in the instant Petition, the Petitioners have sought permission for withdrawal of the present Petition with liberty to approach the Commission in case there is any change in the position communicated by CTUIL.

7. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsels for the parties and the Petitioner’s Memo dated 8.6.2026, the Petitioners are permitted to withdraw the present Petition.

In the instant case, the Petitioner has not paid the transmission charges to PGCIL, leading to the regulation of power by PGCIL. When the Petitioner has not paid the transmission charges to PGCIL, there was no occasion for PTC to reimburse the same to the Petitioner. Therefore, we tend to agree with UPPCL’s

35. In response, UPPCL has submitted that in compliance with the Commission’s directions in Petition No.77/MP/2018, the Petitioner raised a Supplementary Bill reconciling penalties for the period from December 2016 to March 2019. This was duly approved by UPPCL, including the liability towards LPS, and hence no anomaly exists in the levy of penalties. UPPCL has submitted that there is no default on the part of the Discoms under the Procurer-PPA with respect to the Petitioner’s claims. Consequently, the relief sought regarding the payment of LPS has no merit. UPPCL has further submitted that the Petitioner’s claim for losses arising from curtailment of power by PGCIL is not attributable to any act or omission on its part under the Procurers’ PPA. There is no default on the part of the Discoms under the Procurers’ PPA in relation to the claims raised by the Petitioner. Accordingly, the relief sought by the Petitioner towards LPS should not be allowed.

38. We have already held that the Petitioner is not eligible for additional Capacity Charges and a refund of the penalty claimed for the period from January, 2019 to March, 2019. We have also held that the penalty paid “during earlier months” has already been taken care of in the reconciliation carried out by the parties as per the Commission’s directions in the order dated 14.5.2019 in Petition No.77/MP/2018. Therefore, the Petitioner’s prayer for LPS has become infructuous.
